sections.html: Africa: Western and central Africa: Congo River basin, Democratic Republic of the Congo and Central African Republic, and Angola. Type locality: Stanleyville, Congo.

Typically found in fastest flowing portions of rivers and always associated with large rocks; appears to congregate underneath rocks near where water breaks over the rocks during the day, and will move out onto the tops of rocks at night.
These catfish do not possess a swim bladder so they keep away from open waters.

Congoglanis alula differs from C. inga in having a shorter maxillary barbel not reaching to vertical through anterior margin of orbit, a longer pelvic fin (24–28% of standard length vs. 19–21%), a shorter postorbital length, a relatively narrow interorbital width and shorter anal-fin rays. It differs from C. sagitta in having a longer pectoral fin, a longer pelvic fin, a shorter and deeper caudal peduncle, a narrower interorbital width, a more posteriorly placed anal fin and fewer vertebrae (36–39 vs. 39–41). Dorsal soft rays: 8; anal soft rays: 9–11.

The specific name alula means winglet, perhaps referring to flattened and expanded wing-like fins, an adaptation to fast water.

IUCN Red List: Least Concern.
